footnotes: From pre-tax income to net income to American Healthcare REIT: includes a $22.2M income tax benefit; after $1.0M attributable to noncontrolling interests. The data provider reports no separate capital expenditures, so free cash flow equals operating cash flow. Operating income follows StockAnalysis, which places unusual items below the operating line: −$49.9M asset writedowns, $14.6M gains/losses on investments, −$3.0M gains/losses on asset sales in 2025; −$5.5M merger & restructuring charges, −$45.8M asset writedowns, $5.2M gains/losses on asset sales in 2024 (signs as reported: negative = charge).

Figures are from StockAnalysis (S&P Global Market Intelligence data) for fiscal years ended Dec 31, 2025 and a year earlier; free cash flow = operating cash flow − capital expenditures. Never estimated: items not reported there are left out.
Diluted EPS by quarter as reported in the 10-Qs; fourth quarters are calculated (net income ÷ estimated diluted shares) because EPS does not add across quarters.
Percentages are of revenue; figures may not sum due to rounding.

summary: American Healthcare REIT owns senior housing, skilled nursing and outpatient medical properties. Revenue rose 9.4% to $2.3B in 2025. Operating income rose 28.5% to $167M, a 7.4% margin.

Net income was $69.8M, or $0.42 per share, after a $37.8M loss a year earlier. Operating cash flow was $294M and free cash flow $294M, versus $176M; American Healthcare REIT returned $166M through dividends and buybacks.
watch: Net income includes a $22.2M tax benefit.
